utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The proceedings are delayed this afternoon again because the courtroom wasn't emptied on time from the morning session. The Trial Chamber will go ahead and deliver its ruling on protective measures for the next Prosecution witness. The Prosecution witness listed publicly -- was listed publicly throughout the pre-trial proceedings. For reasons stated by the Prosecution on behalf of the witness, it has become necessary that the witness be heard in closed session with a pseudonym. On the submissions of the Defence regarding protective measures, the Trial Chamber is not satisfied that any prejudice will be occasioned to the accused or indeed that any of the rights of the accused will be undermined. There is nothing that has been demonstrated by the Defence that may lead to an unfair trial. While the public nature of a hearing in a criminal trial is to be preferred, the changing circumstances of the witnesses while the witness -- the witnesses make an effort to sustain a livelihood for themselves and their families, if such efforts invite insecurity in any form vis-a-vis their duty to give evidence to the Tribunal, as has been demonstrated in this case, the Trial Chamber has to give due consideration to such insecurity in the status of that witness. The provisions of the Statute in Articles 21 and 22 have sufficiently been explained in the jurisprudence of the Tribunal. The Trial Chamber is satisfied that this is an exceptional case and the protective measures are granted, as requested. The witness shall have a pseudonym "N," and he shall give evidence in closed session. The Trial Chamber is reiterating the need for all parties to these proceedings, including all witnesses and the accused, their families and associates, to abide by the Trial Chamber orders on the protection of witnesses. Nobody must incite any person to attack witnesses or to deal with witnesses unfairly in any other matter that witnesses may be involved in outside the Tribunal, especially in their countries of origin or residence. Otherwise, contempt proceedings will be pursued under Rule 77. The other matter raised by Mr. Zecevic on the summaries provided during pre-trial and those provided just before the witness is called by the Prosecution has been raised before. The Prosecution has been advised how they should handle those problems. The summaries that are supposed to be provided during pre-trial stage are supposed to be detailed. How else can an accused person be said to have had an opportunity to prepare his defence when, in fact, such right is undermined by the Prosecution's lack of diligence in making sure that the accused is not mislaid by being surprised with new material details. If at any stage the Trial Chamber finds that there are new details which are material to the Defence which have not been disclosed before, the Trial Chamber will take appropriate action. And this habit, if repeated by the Prosecution, may lead to undermining the Prosecution case altogether, because it is likely to lead to an unfair trial to the accused. It is very important that in these proceedings in the Tribunal, where investigators have to go to another country to make their investigations, to prepare their defence and even to prepare the Prosecution case, it is important that the Rules of Procedure -- the rules and preparations for trial are complied with strictly. The proceedings will continue as stated in closed session, and the witness can be brought in. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we are waiting for the witness, may I use the time to inform the Trial Chamber that my co-counsel, Ms. Catharine Baen, will be here on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So the matters which she's supposed to raise will be adjourned until --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Because I promised the Trial Chamber that I will inform accordingly today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- at the beginning of the proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, yesterday, counsel for the Defence raised the issue of some outstanding exhibits that had to be dealt with. I can do that now if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Or I can do it later. I'm at the Trial Chamber's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think let's deal with them now in case they have to be discussed by the witnesses. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Can I indicate that as far as the documents which have been marked for identification, being D22A/2 through to D22I/2, that collection of documents, the Prosecution has no objection to their being granted full exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And before we proceed, can we just have confirmation from the registry that they will retain the numbers -- the same numbers as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, they will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I understand that there are three further translations that have been provided. Now, full admission into evidence is being sought by Mr. Lukic in respect of D17/3, D25/3, and D26/3. The Prosecution has no objection to those documents being fully admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have confirmation again that they will retain the same numbers -- oh, before we do that, Mr. Lukic, is there any -- we are discussing D17/3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to submit copies of those documents. I wanted to give them to the usher so he could -- so these are the same documents that the Prosecutor is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. I think we'll get them -- maybe the usher can come and get the documents from Mr. Lukic. Yes we can go ahead with the next witness. MR. DI FAZIO: There is a further issue that concerns Mr. Lukic, and that is the D22/3/ter, which is a document produced by one of the protected witnesses. Mr. Lukic has obtained the original of that particular document and wishes to substitute that original for the document that currently takes the place of D22/3/ter. The Prosecution has no objection to that original being substituted in the place of the document that now forms the basis of D22/3/ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe -- MR. DI FAZIO: And its full admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we can have that. Has it been handed in, the actual original? Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I submitted the original to a representative of the Registry. We were just waiting then for the Prosecution to receive the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have confirmation of the number as an exhibit now. D22/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D22/3 -- or ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And we have the English translation as well. Isn't it? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So the English one is D22/3. Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: And some days ago, I mentioned a number of Prosecution translations that I wanted to produce into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm now in a position to do so. Can I provide, please, P37, P39, P41, and also P38. If I can repeat, P37, P38, P39, and P41. We have copies here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to recollect. These -- we didn't have English translations? MR. DI FAZIO: We didn't have English translations at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And was that the only reason why they were not -- MR. DI FAZIO: That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: Only one matter perhaps that I should mention, and that's in respect of P41. That was ID'ed, I believe. On that occasion when we were dealing with the document, I note from the transcript at page 4511 that Mr. Lukic said that he would not object to the full admission into evidence of that document. It's in fact the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. It relates to the core proceedings relating to one of the protective witnesses. So I'm seeking its full admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure the Defence has is no objection. That is P37, 38, 39, and 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, with all due respect, I was of the impression that we are dealing on the equivalent basis of it here. Because we gave to the Prosecutor -- I gave myself seven days prior to asking the admission just that we can, I mean, look at the documents and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Consider your positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Consider the probable objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I ask my learned colleague if he can give us that and -- MR. DI FAZIO: The case manager informs me that those documents were handed on the first day that we resumed court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry? MR. DI FAZIO: My case manager informs me that those translations were provided, and this accords with my memory too, because I recall standing up on the first day that court resumed, that they were handed to the Defence on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I see the point Mr. Zecevic is raising. It's just that they needed time to be able to regroup their thoughts and instructions. So what we can do is we'll give the Defence time, that we can come back to this even after the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, what I wanted to propose is if we have received - I don't really recall - but if we have received, I have them in -- in -- with other stuff in Defence counsel room and we can inform the Trial Chamber accordingly after the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Any other documents? MR. DI FAZIO: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. So the Trial Chamber will hear from the Defence on P37, P38, P39, and P41 at a later stage when they are ready with stating their opposition. MR. DI FAZIO: If I may be of some assistance to the Defence so that we can hasten this process, they'll find that the documents are dealt with at the following pages in the transcript, P37, if they get their pins --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- page 4304. P38, page 4312 to 4313. P39, page 4314 to 4315. And P41, page 4515 and also page 4511. So they should find --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: -- that in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure that will be very helpful. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we can now proceed. Please bring the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
